title: तिहार कुर्दैन मखमली माला, भदौबाटै विदेश निर्यात
content:
भक्तपुर । तिहार नजिकिएपछि बजारमा फूल तथा मालाको कारोबार बढ्न थाल्छ । तिहारमा विशेषगरी सयपत्री र मखमली फूलको माग बढी हुने गर्छ । चाडपर्वमा हुने मागलाई लक्षित गर्दै काठमाडौं उपत्यकाका किसानहरू मखमली तथा सयपत्री फूलखेतीमा सक्रिय छन्। वर्षौंदेखि व्यवसायिक रुपमा खेती गर्दै आएका किसानहरुका लागि यो राम्रो आम्दानीको माध्यम बनेको छ । ज्ञानेन्द्र थापाले करिब १२–१३ वर्षदेखि व्यावसायिक रूपमा मखमली फूलखेती गर्दै आएका हुन् । उनले अहिले करिब दुई रोपनी क्षेत्रफलमा मखमली फूल लगाएका छन्। पहिले पनि फूल लगाउने गरेकामा पछिल्लो समय यसलाई नियमित व्यवसायका रूपमा अगाडि बढाएको उनले बताए। ‘विगत बर्षदेखि नै फूल रोपण गर्दै आएका हौँ। अहिले करिब दुई रोपनीमा मखमली फूल लगाएका छौँ । व्यवसायिक रूपमा नै अगाडि बढाउँछौँ। प्रत्येक वर्ष उति नै क्षेत्रफलमा खेती गर्छौँ,’ उनले भने। थापाका अनुसार यस वर्ष अघिल्लो वर्षको तुलनामा फूल उत्पादन कम भएको छ। अत्यधिक वर्षा र रोगका कारण फूलका बोट सुक्ने तथा डढ्ने समस्या देखिएको उनले बताए । फूलखेतीमा बीउको गुणस्तरदेखि औषधि तथा विषादीको प्रयोगसम्म ध्यान दिनुपर्ने उनको अनुभव छ । ‘यसवर्ष धेरै फूल डढ्यो, बोट खङ्ग्रङ्ग भयो। बल्लबल्ल फेरि पलाएको छ। पानी धेरै परेपछि फूलको बोट मर्ने समस्या छ । त्यसैले यसपालि पोहोरको तुलनामा फूल कम फुलेको छ,’ उनले भने। उत्पादनमा कमी भए पनि बजारमा फूलको मूल्य भने केही बढेको किसानको भनाइ छ । थापाका अनुसार यस वर्ष मखमली फूलको मूल्य प्रतिमाला ३० देखि ३५ रुपैयाँसम्म पुगेको छ । उनले केही दिनअघि मात्रै प्रतिमाला २५ रुपैयाँमा बिक्री गरेका थिए। थापाले असारको मध्यदेखि नै फूल टिपेर बिक्रीका लागि तयार पार्ने गरेका छन् । साउनको पहिलो तथा दोस्रो सातादेखि माला बाहिरी बजारमा पठाउन थालिन्छ। नेपाली मखमली माला भारत, अस्ट्रेलियालगायत देशमा समेत पुग्ने गरेको उनले बताए। उनका अनुसार एकपटकमा ४० देखि ५० हजारसम्म माला विदेश पठाउने व्यापारीले खरिद गर्ने गरेका छन् । भदौ र असोजसम्म नेपाली मखमली माला विदेश पुगिसक्ने गरेको उनको भनाइ छ । त्यसबाहेक काठमाडौंको कालीमाटी, इमाडोल, पोखरा तथा चितवनलगायत बजारमा समेत माला बिक्री हुने गरेको छ । मखमली फूलको बजार तिहारपछि पनि रहने भएकाले किसानलाई बिक्रीका लागि केही सहज हुने गरेको छ । तिहारपछि पनि बाँकी रहेका माला १० देखि १५ रुपैयाँसम्ममा बिक्री हुने गरेको उनले बताए। यस वर्ष सरकारले भारतीय फूल तथा माला आयातमा प्रतिबन्ध लगाउने वा नलगाउने भन्ने विषयले नेपाली किसानको बजार मूल्य निर्धारणमा प्रभाव पार्ने थापाको अपेक्षा छ। ‘पोहोर भारतबाट फूल ल्याउन प्रतिबन्ध लगाइएको थियो। राम्रो मूल्य पाएका थियौँ। यसपालि पनि भारतबाट फूल ल्याउन बन्द गरियो भने नेपाली किसानले राम्रो भाउ पाउँछन् भन्ने आशा छ,’ उनले भने। त्यस्तै, राधिका थापाले पनि करिब १० वर्षदेखि मखमली फूलखेती गर्दै आएकी छन्। सुरुमा धानखेतका आलीमा फूल रोपेर खेती सुरु गरेकी उनले अहिले घरबारीमै फूल लगाउँदै आएकी छन्। फूलखेतीबाट राम्रो आम्दानी हुन थालेपछि यसलाई निरन्तरता दिएको उनले बताइन्। राधिकाका अनुसार अहिले मखमली मालाको मूल्य प्रतिगोटा २५ रुपैयाँ छ । केही समयअघि २१ रुपैयाँमा बिक्री भइरहेको माला तिहार नजिकिँदै गर्दा क्रमशः महँगो हुँदै गएको उनको भनाइ छ। ‘मैंले फूलखेती गर्न थालेको करिब १० वर्ष भयो। सुरुमा धान रोपेको खेतका आलीमा लगाउँथ्यौँ। अहिले घरमै लगाउन थालेका छौँ। व्यापार राम्रो भएकाले यसलाई निरन्तरता दिएका हौँ। अहिले एउटा मालाको २५ रुपैयाँ दिइरहेका छन्। तिहार नजिकिँदै जाँदा मूल्य अझै बढ्छ भन्ने आशा छ,’ उनले भनिन्। राधिकाका अनुसार मखमली माला काठमाडौंमा मात्रै सीमित छैन। साउन–भदौदेखि नै व्यापारीले माला संकलन गरेर अस्ट्रेलिया, जापान र अमेरिकालगायत देशमा पठाउने गरेका छन्। विदेशमा रहेका नेपाली समुदायले समेत मखमली मालाको माग गर्ने भएकाले यसको बजार विस्तार भएको उनको भनाइ छ। उनले उत्पादन गरेको माला कालीमाटी, इमाडोल, पोखरा र चितवनलगायत बजारमा पनि पुग्ने गरेको छ। फूलको उत्पादन र बिक्रीको परिमाणअनुसार आम्दानी फरक पर्ने भए पनि यस वर्ष उनले मखमली फूलखेतीबाट ७० देखि ८० हजार रुपैयाँसम्म आम्दानी गरेको बताइन्। उनका अनुसार सयपत्री फूलको बिक्री भने मुख्यतः तिहार लक्षित हुने गरेको छ। कुकुर तिहारदेखि नै सयपत्री फूलको माग बढ्ने र व्यापारीले अर्डर गर्न थाल्ने गर्छन्। मखमली माला भने तिहारअघि नै विदेश पठाउने तथा तिहारपछि पनि बिक्री गर्न सकिने भएकाले यसको बजार तुलनात्मक रूपमा लामो समयसम्म रहने गरेको उनले बताइन्। सानो क्षेत्रफलबाट सुरु भएको फूलखेती अहिले किसानका लागि आम्दानीको माध्यम बनेको छ। विदेशमा समेत नेपाली मखमली मालाको माग बढ्दै जानुले फूलखेतीलाई व्यावसायिक रूपमा विस्तार गर्ने सम्भावना देखाएको छ। तर उत्पादनमा मौसमको प्रभाव, रोगको प्रकोप र आयातित फूलसँगको प्रतिस्पर्धा किसानका लागि चुनौतीका रूपमा रहेका छन्। –प्रमिला कार्की/NNB Bhaktapur. As Tihar approaches, the business of flowers and garlands starts increasing in the market. During Tihar, the demand for marigolds and velvet flowers is especially high. Farmers in the Kathmandu Valley are actively cultivating velvet and centaury flowers, targeting the demand during the festive season. This has become a good source of income for farmers who have been cultivating them commercially for years. Gyanendra Thapa has been cultivating velvet flowers commercially for about 12-13 years. He has currently planted velvet flowers in an area of about two ropanis. He said that he had been cultivating flowers before, but recently he has taken it up as a regular business. "We have been planting flowers since last year. We have now planted velvet flowers in about two ropanis. We are doing it commercially. We cultivate the same area every year," he said. According to Thapa, this year's flower production has been lower than last year. He said that due to excessive rainfall and diseases, flower plants have been drying up and burning. He has experience that in floriculture, attention should be paid to everything from the quality of seeds to the use of medicines and pesticides. "This year, many flowers were burnt, the plants became stunted. They are slowly growing again. There is a problem of flower plants dying after too much rain. That is why the flowers have bloomed less this year compared to last year," he said. Despite the decrease in production, the price of flowers in the market has increased somewhat, according to farmers. According to Thapa, the price of velvet flowers this year has reached Rs 30 to 35 per piece. He had sold a piece for Rs 25 just a few days ago. Thapa has been picking flowers and preparing them for sale since mid-Ashar. The garlands start being sent to the external market from the first and second weeks of Shrawan. He said that Nepali velvet garlands even reach countries including India and Australia. According to him, traders who send 40,000 to 50,000 garlands abroad buy them at a time. He says that Nepali velvet garlands reach abroad by Bhadra and Asoj. Apart from that, garlands are also sold in markets including Kalimati, Imadol, Pokhara and Chitwan in Kathmandu. The market for velvet flowers continues even after Tihar, making it easier for farmers to sell. He said that even after Tihar, the remaining garlands are sold for between Rs 10 and Rs 15. Thapa expects that the issue of whether or not the government will ban the import of Indian flowers and garlands this year will have an impact on the market price determination of Nepali farmers. "Last year, there was a ban on importing flowers from India. We got good prices. If the ban on importing flowers from India is lifted this year too, we hope that Nepali farmers will get good prices," he said. Similarly, Radhika Thapa has also been cultivating velvet flowers for about 10 years. She initially started by planting flowers in the paddy fields and is now growing flowers in her own garden. She said that she has continued this since she started earning good income from flower cultivation. According to Radhika, the current price of velvet garlands is Rs 25 per piece. She says that garlands, which were being sold for Rs 21 some time ago, are gradually becoming more expensive as Tihar approaches. "I started growing flowers about 10 years ago. Initially, we used to grow them in the fields where rice is planted. Now we have started growing them at home. We have continued it because business is good. Currently, they are offering Rs 25 for a garland. I hope the price will increase further as Tihar approaches," she said. According to Radhika, velvet garlands are not limited to Kathmandu. Since Shrawan-Bhadra, traders have been collecting garlands and sending them to countries including Australia, Japan, and the US. She says that the market for velvet garlands has expanded as the Nepali community abroad is also demanding it. The garlands she produces reach markets in Kalimati, Imadol, Pokhara, and Chitwan. Although her income varies depending on the volume of flower production and sales, she said that this year she earned between 70,000 and 80,000 rupees from her velvet flower farming. According to her, the sale of centipede flowers is mainly targeted for Tihar. The demand for centipede flowers increases from Kukur Tihar onwards and traders start placing orders. As for velvet garlands, they are sent abroad before Tihar and can be sold even after Tihar, so their market remains relatively long, she said. Floriculture, which started from a small area, has now become a source of income for farmers. The increasing demand for Nepali velvet garlands even abroad has shown the potential to expand floriculture commercially. However, the impact of weather on production, disease outbreaks, and competition with imported flowers remain challenges for farmers. –Pramila Karki/NNB

‘पोहोर भारतबाट फूल ल्याउन प्रतिबन्ध लगाइएको थियो। राम्रो मूल्य पाएका थियौँ। यसपालि पनि भारतबाट फूल ल्याउन बन्द गरियो भने नेपाली किसानले राम्रो भाउ पाउँछन् भन्ने आशा छ,’ उनले भने। त्यस्तै, राधिका थापाले पनि करिब १० वर्षदेखि मखमली फूलखेती गर्दै आएकी छन्। सुरुमा धानखेतका आलीमा फूल रोपेर खेती सुरु गरेकी उनले अहिले घरबारीमै फूल लगाउँदै आएकी छन्। फूलखेतीबाट राम्रो आम्दानी हुन थालेपछि यसलाई निरन्तरता दिएको उनले बताइन्। राधिकाका अनुसार अहिले मखमली मालाको मूल्य प्रतिगोटा २५ रुपैयाँ छ । केही समयअघि २१ रुपैयाँमा बिक्री भइरहेको माला तिहार नजिकिँदै गर्दा क्रमशः महँगो हुँदै गएको उनको भनाइ छ। ‘मैंले फूलखेती गर्न थालेको करिब १० वर्ष भयो। सुरुमा धान रोपेको खेतका आलीमा लगाउँथ्यौँ। अहिले घरमै लगाउन थालेका छौँ। व्यापार राम्रो भएकाले यसलाई निरन्तरता दिएका हौँ। अहिले एउटा मालाको २५ रुपैयाँ दिइरहेका छन्। तिहार नजिकिँदै जाँदा मूल्य अझै बढ्छ भन्ने आशा छ,’ उनले भनिन्। राधिकाका अनुसार मखमली माला काठमाडौंमा मात्रै सीमित छैन। साउन–भदौदेखि नै व्यापारीले माला संकलन गरेर अस्ट्रेलिया, जापान र अमेरिकालगायत देशमा पठाउने गरेका छन्। विदेशमा रहेका नेपाली समुदायले समेत मखमली मालाको माग गर्ने भएकाले यसको बजार विस्तार भएको उनको भनाइ छ। उनले उत्पादन गरेको माला कालीमाटी, इमाडोल, पोखरा र चितवनलगायत बजारमा पनि पुग्ने गरेको छ। फूलको उत्पादन र बिक्रीको परिमाणअनुसार आम्दानी फरक पर्ने भए पनि यस वर्ष उनले मखमली फूलखेतीबाट ७० देखि ८० हजार रुपैयाँसम्म आम्दानी गरेको बताइन्। उनका अनुसार सयपत्री फूलको बिक्री भने मुख्यतः तिहार लक्षित हुने गरेको छ। कुकुर तिहारदेखि नै सयपत्री फूलको माग बढ्ने र व्यापारीले अर्डर गर्न थाल्ने गर्छन्। मखमली माला भने तिहारअघि नै विदेश पठाउने तथा तिहारपछि पनि बिक्री गर्न सकिने भएकाले यसको बजार तुलनात्मक रूपमा लामो समयसम्म रहने गरेको उनले बताइन्। सानो क्षेत्रफलबाट सुरु भएको फूलखेती अहिले किसानका लागि आम्दानीको माध्यम बनेको छ। विदेशमा समेत नेपाली मखमली मालाको माग बढ्दै जानुले फूलखेतीलाई व्यावसायिक रूपमा विस्तार गर्ने सम्भावना देखाएको छ। तर उत्पादनमा मौसमको प्रभाव, रोगको प्रकोप र आयातित फूलसँगको प्रतिस्पर्धा किसानका लागि चुनौतीका रूपमा रहेका छन्। –प्रमिला कार्की/NNB

भक्तपुर । तिहार नजिकिएपछि बजारमा फूल तथा मालाको कारोबार बढ्न थाल्छ । तिहारमा विशेषगरी सयपत्री र मखमली फूलको माग बढी हुने गर्छ ।

चाडपर्वमा हुने मागलाई लक्षित गर्दै काठमाडौं उपत्यकाका किसानहरू मखमली तथा सयपत्री फूलखेतीमा सक्रिय छन्। वर्षौंदेखि व्यवसायिक रुपमा खेती गर्दै आएका किसानहरुका लागि यो राम्रो आम्दानीको माध्यम बनेको छ ।

ज्ञानेन्द्र थापाले करिब १२–१३ वर्षदेखि व्यावसायिक रूपमा मखमली फूलखेती गर्दै आएका हुन् । उनले अहिले करिब दुई रोपनी क्षेत्रफलमा मखमली फूल लगाएका छन्। पहिले पनि फूल लगाउने गरेकामा पछिल्लो समय यसलाई नियमित व्यवसायका रूपमा अगाडि बढाएको उनले बताए।

‘विगत बर्षदेखि नै फूल रोपण गर्दै आएका हौँ। अहिले करिब दुई रोपनीमा मखमली फूल लगाएका छौँ । व्यवसायिक रूपमा नै अगाडि बढाउँछौँ। प्रत्येक वर्ष उति नै क्षेत्रफलमा खेती गर्छौँ,’ उनले भने।

थापाका अनुसार यस वर्ष अघिल्लो वर्षको तुलनामा फूल उत्पादन कम भएको छ। अत्यधिक वर्षा र रोगका कारण फूलका बोट सुक्ने तथा डढ्ने समस्या देखिएको उनले बताए । फूलखेतीमा बीउको गुणस्तरदेखि औषधि तथा विषादीको प्रयोगसम्म ध्यान दिनुपर्ने उनको अनुभव छ ।

‘यसवर्ष धेरै फूल डढ्यो, बोट खङ्ग्रङ्ग भयो। बल्लबल्ल फेरि पलाएको छ। पानी धेरै परेपछि फूलको बोट मर्ने समस्या छ । त्यसैले यसपालि पोहोरको तुलनामा फूल कम फुलेको छ,’ उनले भने।

उत्पादनमा कमी भए पनि बजारमा फूलको मूल्य भने केही बढेको किसानको भनाइ छ । थापाका अनुसार यस वर्ष मखमली फूलको मूल्य प्रतिमाला ३० देखि ३५ रुपैयाँसम्म पुगेको छ । उनले केही दिनअघि मात्रै प्रतिमाला २५ रुपैयाँमा बिक्री गरेका थिए।

उनका अनुसार एकपटकमा ४० देखि ५० हजारसम्म माला विदेश पठाउने व्यापारीले खरिद गर्ने गरेका छन् । भदौ र असोजसम्म नेपाली मखमली माला विदेश पुगिसक्ने गरेको उनको भनाइ छ । त्यसबाहेक काठमाडौंको कालीमाटी, इमाडोल, पोखरा तथा चितवनलगायत बजारमा समेत माला बिक्री हुने गरेको छ ।

Bhaktapur. As Tihar approaches, the business of flowers and garlands starts increasing in the market. During Tihar, the demand for marigolds and velvet flowers is especially high. Farmers in the Kathmandu Valley are actively cultivating velvet and centaury flowers, targeting the demand during the festive season. This has become a good source of income for farmers who have been cultivating them commercially for years. Gyanendra Thapa has been cultivating velvet flowers commercially for about 12-13 years. He has currently planted velvet flowers in an area of about two ropanis. He said that he had been cultivating flowers before, but recently he has taken it up as a regular business. "We have been planting flowers since last year. We have now planted velvet flowers in about two ropanis. We are doing it commercially. We cultivate the same area every year," he said. According to Thapa, this year's flower production has been lower than last year. He said that due to excessive rainfall and diseases, flower plants have been drying up and burning. He has experience that in floriculture, attention should be paid to everything from the quality of seeds to the use of medicines and pesticides. "This year, many flowers were burnt, the plants became stunted. They are slowly growing again. There is a problem of flower plants dying after too much rain. That is why the flowers have bloomed less this year compared to last year," he said. Despite the decrease in production, the price of flowers in the market has increased somewhat, according to farmers. According to Thapa, the price of velvet flowers this year has reached Rs 30 to 35 per piece. He had sold a piece for Rs 25 just a few days ago. Thapa has been picking flowers and preparing them for sale since mid-Ashar. The garlands start being sent to the external market from the first and second weeks of Shrawan. He said that Nepali velvet garlands even reach countries including India and Australia. According to him, traders who send 40,000 to 50,000 garlands abroad buy them at a time. He says that Nepali velvet garlands reach abroad by Bhadra and Asoj. Apart from that, garlands are also sold in markets including Kalimati, Imadol, Pokhara and Chitwan in Kathmandu. The market for velvet flowers continues even after Tihar, making it easier for farmers to sell. He said that even after Tihar, the remaining garlands are sold for between Rs 10 and Rs 15. Thapa expects that the issue of whether or not the government will ban the import of Indian flowers and garlands this year will have an impact on the market price determination of Nepali farmers. "Last year, there was a ban on importing flowers from India. We got good prices. If the ban on importing flowers from India is lifted this year too, we hope that Nepali farmers will get good prices," he said. Similarly, Radhika Thapa has also been cultivating velvet flowers for about 10 years. She initially started by planting flowers in the paddy fields and is now growing flowers in her own garden. She said that she has continued this since she started earning good income from flower cultivation. According to Radhika, the current price of velvet garlands is Rs 25 per piece. She says that garlands, which were being sold for Rs 21 some time ago, are gradually becoming more expensive as Tihar approaches. "I started growing flowers about 10 years ago. Initially, we used to grow them in the fields where rice is planted. Now we have started growing them at home. We have continued it because business is good. Currently, they are offering Rs 25 for a garland. I hope the price will increase further as Tihar approaches," she said. According to Radhika, velvet garlands are not limited to Kathmandu. Since Shrawan-Bhadra, traders have been collecting garlands and sending them to countries including Australia, Japan, and the US. She says that the market for velvet garlands has expanded as the Nepali community abroad is also demanding it. The garlands she produces reach markets in Kalimati, Imadol, Pokhara, and Chitwan. Although her income varies depending on the volume of flower production and sales, she said that this year she earned between 70,000 and 80,000 rupees from her velvet flower farming. According to her, the sale of centipede flowers is mainly targeted for Tihar. The demand for centipede flowers increases from Kukur Tihar onwards and traders start placing orders. As for velvet garlands, they are sent abroad before Tihar and can be sold even after Tihar, so their market remains relatively long, she said. Floriculture, which started from a small area, has now become a source of income for farmers. The increasing demand for Nepali velvet garlands even abroad has shown the potential to expand floriculture commercially. However, the impact of weather on production, disease outbreaks, and competition with imported flowers remain challenges for farmers. –Pramila Karki/NNB

Farmers in the Kathmandu Valley are actively cultivating velvet and centaury flowers, targeting the demand during the festive season. This has become a good source of income for farmers who have been cultivating them commercially for years.

Gyanendra Thapa has been cultivating velvet flowers commercially for about 12-13 years. He has currently planted velvet flowers in an area of about two ropanis. He said that he had been cultivating flowers before, but recently he has taken it up as a regular business.

"We have been planting flowers since last year. We have now planted velvet flowers in about two ropanis. We are doing it commercially. We cultivate the same area every year," he said.

According to Thapa, this year's flower production has been lower than last year. He said that due to excessive rainfall and diseases, flower plants have been drying up and burning. He has experience that in floriculture, attention should be paid to everything from the quality of seeds to the use of medicines and pesticides.

"This year, many flowers were burnt, the plants became stunted. They are slowly growing again. There is a problem of flower plants dying after too much rain. That is why the flowers have bloomed less this year compared to last year," he said.

Despite the decrease in production, the price of flowers in the market has increased somewhat, according to farmers. According to Thapa, the price of velvet flowers this year has reached Rs 30 to 35 per piece. He had sold a piece for Rs 25 just a few days ago.

Thapa has been picking flowers and preparing them for sale since mid-Ashar. The garlands start being sent to the external market from the first and second weeks of Shrawan. He said that Nepali velvet garlands even reach countries including India and Australia.

According to him, traders who send 40,000 to 50,000 garlands abroad buy them at a time. He says that Nepali velvet garlands reach abroad by Bhadra and Asoj. Apart from that, garlands are also sold in markets including Kalimati, Imadol, Pokhara and Chitwan in Kathmandu.

The market for velvet flowers continues even after Tihar, making it easier for farmers to sell. He said that even after Tihar, the remaining garlands are sold for between Rs 10 and Rs 15.

Thapa expects that the issue of whether or not the government will ban the import of Indian flowers and garlands this year will have an impact on the market price determination of Nepali farmers.

"Last year, there was a ban on importing flowers from India. We got good prices. If the ban on importing flowers from India is lifted this year too, we hope that Nepali farmers will get good prices," he said.

Similarly, Radhika Thapa has also been cultivating velvet flowers for about 10 years. She initially started by planting flowers in the paddy fields and is now growing flowers in her own garden. She said that she has continued this since she started earning good income from flower cultivation.

According to Radhika, the current price of velvet garlands is Rs 25 per piece. She says that garlands, which were being sold for Rs 21 some time ago, are gradually becoming more expensive as Tihar approaches.

"I started growing flowers about 10 years ago. Initially, we used to grow them in the fields where rice is planted. Now we have started growing them at home. We have continued it because business is good. Currently, they are offering Rs 25 for a garland. I hope the price will increase further as Tihar approaches," she said.

According to Radhika, velvet garlands are not limited to Kathmandu. Since Shrawan-Bhadra, traders have been collecting garlands and sending them to countries including Australia, Japan, and the US. She says that the market for velvet garlands has expanded as the Nepali community abroad is also demanding it.

The garlands she produces reach markets in Kalimati, Imadol, Pokhara, and Chitwan. Although her income varies depending on the volume of flower production and sales, she said that this year she earned between 70,000 and 80,000 rupees from her velvet flower farming.

According to her, the sale of centipede flowers is mainly targeted for Tihar. The demand for centipede flowers increases from Kukur Tihar onwards and traders start placing orders. As for velvet garlands, they are sent abroad before Tihar and can be sold even after Tihar, so their market remains relatively long, she said.

Floriculture, which started from a small area, has now become a source of income for farmers. The increasing demand for Nepali velvet garlands even abroad has shown the potential to expand floriculture commercially. However, the impact of weather on production, disease outbreaks, and competition with imported flowers remain challenges for farmers. –Pramila Karki/NNB
